contentList.content: Show me. Put my fingers where they go.
Two: sleep with your boots on the first night in a new camp. In case you have to run.
Tell me about her instead.
Keeping your boots on is sensible. I sleep in mine too.
I'm glad you're with us.
*[The Urge] The string at her throat. One move - and the song is over.*
Because someone has to.
...There. That's a chord. Don't - don't look at me like that, you'll lose it.
Oh. It's you. I'll admit - you did help me finish it. I haven't decided yet what to make of you.
Who said I do it for free?
I hope you never let a fighter carry it.
It's not the running. It's that last time I didn't have my boots on. Lihala did. She... she told me to go.
Right behind you.
*She notices nothing, and plays on.*
Let's.
Never sleep next to Astarion.
Are you going to glow like that all night?
Play the chord.
Oh - no, of course. The offer stands. I'll be here. Composing. Probably badly.
Two tieflings walk into a goblin camp... no, I'm not finishing that joke. But yes. Yes, we should.
I'll keep the fire going.
What rules?
...You can't promise that. But it's nice that you tried.
And three - never, ever let the fighter carry the lute.
Tell me about Lihala.
Maybe. Twelve is a good number. Unfinished is a good song, sometimes.
The squirrels have terrible taste. Everyone knows that. ...They did go quiet at the end, though. I'm choosing to count that.
*She plays something simple, something bright.*
...Thank you. I needed someone to say it who isn't me.
One: never play the sad song first. Make them laugh, then make them cry, then pass the hat.
You can't just say things like that.
Oh - hi. Don't mind me. I'm just... counting.
Your turn. Everyone on the road has a rule. What's yours?
You all right? You look like you've seen a ghost.
She'd be proud of you.
I don't know how.
*She tips her head back towards the sky.*
A bard never turns down another bard.
You're no fighter.
Never. Rule three. I'd sooner hand it to an owlbear.
She'd have liked you. She'd have yelled at you too, mind - she yelled at everyone she liked.
No.
The thirteenth was going to be Baldur's Gate. She had the knife out on the road. She was going to cut it early, for luck.
...We'll work on it. Lihala would've made you play 'til your fingers bled.
Take it back. It's yours.
Why me, of all people?
Here? The Grove... yes. Yes, it does, doesn't it. It's where I finished her song.
Since Elturel I've slept in a heap of tieflings. Dozens of us - someone's tail always in my face, someone always snoring. ...It's too quiet out here. I can hear myself think. I don't like it.
You. You sang that line like you'd known her. I still can't get over it.
Must reek something awful.
...Then I'll make sure they remember you. Whatever happens.
Ha! No, that one was every night.
Rude. Accurate, but rude.
So's a bow. Go tell a ranger that.
Can I ask you something? For the song, obviously. Why do you do it? All of this - helping people you don't even know.
There's a tadpole in my head. If I don't make it, I want someone to.
Goodnight, Alfira.
I can insult a goblin so badly it actually hurts - that's a real spell, don't laugh. And I know a few words that close wounds.
Probably. Lihala said I only had two settings: glowing and sulking. You're getting the good one.
Oh, good. Then we can be ready to flee together. Very romantic.
*A pause. She looks down at her boots.*
*She draws her knees up to her chest, boots right by the fire.*
Can I ask you something odd? Do you still have her lute? I - I'd just like to see it.
Changed your mind? I won't say I told you so. Out loud.
If you could go anywhere, where would you go?
I keep thinking about what you asked me. What would I say to her. Turns out I had a whole song's worth.
What? I'm fine. Perfectly fine. Why are you looking at me like that?
A soft heart behind a price tag. I can work with that. It rhymes with everything.
What's the point of a eulogy, anyway?
*She plays something simple, something bright.*
*She sits hugging the lute to her chest, running a finger along its neck.*
What does that lute mean to you?
Have the squirrels stopped complaining about your singing?
I'd rather listen to you.
What can you do in a fight?
It's just wood and strings.
Then I'll just have to be the exception. Lihala always said I was stubborn.
*She takes your hand - and holds it a moment longer than she needs to.*
Resist. Listen to the music.
Cut the thirteenth when we reach the city. Together.
We tieflings should stick together.
Fingers here. No - here. Lihala did this to me for a year.
Oh, the ballads hate modest heroes. I'll fix you in the chorus.
*She hums along without words, and falls asleep halfway through a verse.*
Not now.
Noted. Underlined. Twice.
Listen.
Right. Of course, heroes, busy - wait. Wait, just - one thing.
Shall we dance?
Clench your fist. Say nothing.
What are you counting?
Trust no one.
...I've slept with my boots on every night since Elturel.
Lighter. Like I put down a pack I'd been carrying since the road.
It's dangerous out there. Are you sure?
There they are - my accompanist! I've been humming that bridge all morning. Lihala would've said I'm insufferable.
Mattis is going to be furious I didn't say goodbye properly. I'll write him a song. He'll hate it. He'll hum it for a week.
Early start tomorrow. Get some sleep.
I just keep ending up in the wrong place at the right time.
All right, all right - come along.
A bard is just another mouth to feed.
...Is it that obvious? I'm terrified. I've been terrified since the road. I just - I'm tired of being terrified sitting still.
...You made me miss a note. Nobody's made me miss a note since I was twelve.
Try to understand what's really behind it.
Watch her, not the strings.
She'd want it played, not hung on a wall. And you play it better than I would right now. Don't tell anyone I said that.
Lihala cut one for every town we played. Twelve. Beregost, Nashkel, a pig farm she swore was a town...
...Oh. That's a good one. That's a really good one. I'm stealing it.
Play her something to fall asleep to.
I'll find your camp and wait for you there.
Let me guess - never sing off-key?
Hah. That's a verse right there. Simple. Stubborn. I like it.
I eat very little. Mostly my own words, lately.
*Half-asleep, she sits up and slowly pulls off her boots. She sets them beside her. For the first time since Elturel.*
Stop it. No - actually, don't stop, I could get used to this.
Tonight? Making sure you don't get cold.
How are you holding up?
Bit late for that, isn't it? I'm about to sleep ten feet from you.
Can't sleep? First night away from your people.
Cut it now. The Grove counts.
I should go.
Maybe it's better left as it is.
*She stumbles half a note.*
That was terrible. Truly awful. Again!
Say please.
...That one's not going in the song.
You sang beautifully. Truly.
I'm glad you're with us.
Never fall asleep next to strangers.
Two left feet and not a care in the world. That's where the first line came from. Dance upon the stars tonight.
*Half-asleep, she sits up and slowly pulls off her boots. She sets them beside her. For the first time since Elturel.*
Always go back for your own.
*She turns the neck towards the fire. A row of small notches runs along it.*
Strike first.
It's just a habit. Forget it.
*When the song ends, she smiles to herself.*
You won't have to run here.
...Deal. And you're holding the knife steady, because my hands will be shaking.
Lihala had rules for the road. First night out, she'd make me recite them. Every. Single. Time.
A duet. On the road. Oh, Lihala would have loved this.
Right. No - that's fair. That's... fair. Thank you anyway. For the song.
Our first night on the road, I woke up to this awful thumping. Thought it was bandits.
Look at her more closely.
Here? Now? With - ...One dance. Badly. In her honour.
Me too. I keep counting heads - you, the fire, the others. Old habit from the road.
